claims.statement: PPWR entered into force on 11 February 2025 and applies generally from 12 August 2026 across packaging materials and origins.
Packaging must meet recyclability grades from 2030 or later if delegated acts are delayed, while fee modulation follows the relevant delegated and implementing acts.
German reporting requires material type, component weight and verifiable determination; estimates alone are insufficient.
German domestic producers generally must submit their own data reports, so software should prepare evidence and exports without claiming to assume the legal act of filing.
Dutch 2026 fees vary by material and include additional per-unit SUP charges, supporting a country-specific fee data model.
Poland's BDO provides electronic packaging and product reporting, supporting a locally accessible pilot workflow.
Direct competitors publish self-serve packaging compliance tiers from EUR 29 monthly and a mid-market tier at EUR 299 monthly.

contrary_evidence: The key PPWR design-for-recycling and fee-modulation machinery depends on later delegated and implementing acts, limiting authoritative near-term simulation.
PPWR Connect already advertises declarations, grades, EPR market sheets and API access at published prices, while PackComply targets mid-market FMCG.
German domestic producers generally cannot delegate the filing itself to a broker, limiting a done-for-you submission promise.
National portals and producer-responsibility organisations already provide free registration or reporting interfaces; value must come from upstream data quality and workflow.
Converters may resist a tool that recommends material substitution away from their products.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: a versioned rule-and-evidence graph linked to recurring component classifications and correction patterns, not exclusive ownership of public regulations
fingerprint.customer: mid-market multi-SKU EU consumer brands and importers with fragmented packaging specifications and several national EPR obligations
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: packaging converters, design agencies, producer-responsibility advisers, fractional sustainability teams and product-information implementers
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: packaging BOM version control, supplier evidence requests, rule provenance, national reporting exports, human-approved declarations and explicitly scenario-labelled fee and recyclability analysis
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: a brand group pays onboarding and a recurring workspace fee for governed packaging changes, evidence and country-ready exports
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a component, supplier, market, material or sales-volume change alters evidence, declarations, current fees or future PPWR exposure

founder_fit: Strong FMCG, quantitative modelling, document extraction and Polish/EU adjacency.
A Polish-brand or converter pilot can be delivered part-time with limited public exposure and before multi-country expansion.
Employment conflicts must be avoided: no Reckitt confidential data, supplier terms, work time or proprietary packaging knowledge may be used without permission.
Country-rule maintenance and legal assurance must be contracted once coverage expands.
risks: A scenario estimate can be mistaken for an authoritative fee or legal conclusion.
Rule changes can make grades or fee projections stale.
Incomplete supplier data can produce confident but wrong outputs.
Low-price incumbents can commoditize reporting and simple calculators.
Multi-country legal maintenance can exceed a part-time founder's capacity.
Using employer information or relationships without permission would create conflict and confidentiality risk.

structure.commercial_archetype: packaging specification change-control and evidence software
structure.control_point: the approved packaging specification and evidence pack used before procurement and country reporting
structure.critical_dependency: complete supplier BOMs, current national rules, explicit uncertainty for unfinished PPWR acts and a channel that does not view substitution advice as conflict

thesis: Give multi-country EU brands a versioned packaging bill of materials, supplier-evidence workflow, national reporting mappings and scenario models before a packaging change is approved. The product must distinguish current national fee rules from future PPWR scenarios because the decisive EU recyclability criteria and modulation acts are not all final. Research supports recurring data work but reveals low-priced self-serve competitors, so the defensible wedge is approval workflow, provenance and supplier collaboration rather than a generic compliance calculator.
title: Packaging Change-Control Ledger with Country EPR Evidence
uncertainties: Paid willingness to buy approval workflow above low-cost compliance trackers.
Supplier willingness and ability to provide complete component specifications.
Timing and content of future PPWR delegated and implementing acts.
Reliable access and maintenance burden for national fee schedules and export schemas.
Actual correction cost, sales cycle, retention and country-expansion cost.
